I wanted to like this game, but the lack of balanced matchmaking gives it something I dub the TF2 effect-- where there is a substantial learning curve to the game, but the only way to climb that curve is to lose over and over and over.

Maybe I'm spoiled by games with dedicated servers (league, dota, hots) and good matchmaking algorithms, but I'd much rather win some of my games while not understanding certain mechanics than lose all of my games because I don't understand those mechanics. It really detracts from the gameplay when you almost constantly lose despite trying to play the game, and the only way to win is to dredge strategy information off of unofficial forums and youtube videos.

Not to mention you get flamed for trying to learn the game, told to go to other "noob" servers that also get mad at you for being new. Usually one side has people who know each other and tilt the game so you don't have an impact. If it was popular enough this would not be an issue as the game would be flooded with casuals trying to learn the game, but as is it's only the hard core that play now.

American photojournalist Dickey Chapelle is administered last rites in Viet Nam. She was the first American female reporter to be killed in action. 1965

Dickey Chapelle, born Georgette Louise Meyer (March 14, 1919–November 4, 1965), was an American photojournalist known for her work as a war correspondent from World War II through the Vietnam War.

Chapelle was killed in Vietnam on November 4, 1965 while on patrol with a Marine platoon during Operation Black Ferret, a search and destroy operation. The lieutenant in front of her kicked a tripwire boobytrap, consisting of a mortar shell with a hand grenade attached to the top of it. Chapelle was hit in the neck by a piece of shrapnel which severed her carotid artery; she died soon after. Her last moments were captured in this photograph by Henri Huet. Her body was repatriated with an honor guard consisting of six Marines, and she was given full Marine burial. She became the first female war correspondent to be killed in Vietnam, as well as the first American female reporter to be killed in action.
